title: Coxiella burnetii Real-Time PCR - IS1111a Method (Q Fever)
author: Judy A Northill
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rhhd336
materials: The assay has been optimised and validated for the Rotor-Gene 6000 and Rotor-Gene Q thermocyclers. PCR *Florescence acquisition step

steps.title: Prepare reaction master mix
steps.instruction: Calculate the number of reactions needed and add a dead volume of two extra reactions; dispense 15 µL of SensiFAST Probe Lo‑ROX 2X mix (Bioline, catalog BIO‑84020) into each well of a 100‑place rotor disc on a Rotor‑Gene 6000 or Rotor‑Gene Q 5‑plex.

steps.title: Add template and controls
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of extracted DNA sample, positive control, or no‑template control (nuclease‑free water) to each corresponding well, bringing the total reaction volume to 20 µL.

steps.title: Run PCR assay
steps.instruction: Place the rotor disc in the Rotor‑Gene instrument and run the IS1111a real‑time PCR program as per the instrument’s standard settings (no additional parameters were specified in the source).

steps.title: Interpret amplification results
steps.instruction: Examine each amplification curve for a sigmoidal shape (horizontal baseline, exponential rise, plateau); ensure fluorescence intensity is comparable to the positive control; confirm that the threshold (C_T) is crossed early in the log‑linear phase. A C_T value ≤ 40 cycles is considered positive; C_T > 40 cycles or no curve in the NTC indicates a negative result. NTCs must not produce a curve.
